name: Mark Cuban
role: American entrepreneur, investor, Shark Tank panelist and Cost Plus Drugs co-founder
summary: Cuban describes himself as socially centrist and fiscally conservative, with a libertarian streak, and has backed Democratic presidential candidates since 2016 while calling himself not a fan of either party. His policy focus is healthcare cost transparency and antitrust against large insurers and PBMs, along with a higher minimum wage, free-trade skepticism of tariffs and light regulation of AI.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said in 2026 he is 'not opposed to single-payer or universal healthcare at all' and in 2025 that 'healthcare is a right', while holding that judging a system needs cost transparency and disputing the particulars of Sanders' bill.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In a June 2026 X post he said raising the minimum wage to $20 an hour is the smart choice for businesses and taxpayers.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Praises capitalism and a 'free market or mostly free market' but says the market is 'not always efficient' and that there is a delay.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed in a November 2026 X post raising the top federal income tax bracket from 37% to 44% on earned income and extending Social Security tax to earnings of $1-5 million.

unions-good.rationale: Said he has 'no problem' with unions, called them a win-win with employers, pledged not to oppose unionization at his Cost Plus plant, and would never say 'get rid of unions'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Backs the Break Up Big Medicine Act to separate insurers, PBMs and providers and wants algorithm source code published for youth platforms; also favours light AI regulation.

limit-guns.rationale: Proposed an 'update' to the Second Amendment: every citizen has the right to own a gun, no federal confiscation, states decide purchase and ownership rules.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: On the Lex Fridman podcast he defended diversity programs and said race-conscious measures are legitimate when meant to repair past discrimination, while criticising costly university DEI bureaucracies.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Said in 2019 that sending home highly educated foreigners is 'really stupid' and in 2024 that mass deportation would hurt small businesses, while saying Biden-Harris 'screwed up on immigration' at the border.

free-trade.rationale: Called Trump's across-the-board tariffs a tax on everybody and his trade policy gibberish, a move away from free trade.

basic-income.rationale: Replied in 2017 to a basic-income advocate that it was one of the worst responses to job losses from automation, and said after studying it he was not convinced.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Described Trump's proposed tariffs as 'a tax on everybody'.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said in 2014 that he asks what the problem is and how to solve it rather than starting from an approach, and in 2026 that 'ideology is not a strategy' and policy should not rest on slogans.

taxation-theft.rationale: Said that after military service it is patriotic to pay taxes.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Argued in 2017 that even if one were 99% sure climate change is a hoax, the remaining 1% of uncertainty justifies buying time for technology, so leaving the Paris Agreement was a mistake.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Proposed a higher top income tax bracket of 44% on top of the existing bracket structure, a graduated rather than single-rate income tax.

ban-cartels.rationale: Wants the largest vertically integrated health insurers broken up, calling the structure anti-competitive.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: On the Lex Fridman podcast he said he would not call the Supreme Court's Harvard/North Carolina affirmative action decision a great one, because a diverse student body better prepares students.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Joined the 2015 Texas Wins campaign for protection from discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations, saying he has little tolerance for discrimination in his businesses.

abolish-ip.rationale: Wants software and design patents eliminated and other patents to lapse into the public domain if unused within five years, but not all intellectual property abolished; he also said copyright rules should adapt to AI.

reviewHistory.rationale: Said existing copyright rules should be adapted to the digital age and that AI training needs more than public-domain data, implying IP stays.

free-public-college.rationale: Has argued community college should be free but opposed Clinton's 2016 college plan; mixed.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Said in 2022 'I'm good with the Biden proposal' of $10,000 forgiveness, while opposing full cancellation.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Proposed raising the top federal income tax rate to 44% and said paying taxes is patriotic, so he keeps income tax rather than abolishing it.

notes: Mixed evidence on taxes (patriotic to pay taxes and a 44% top rate versus opposition to unrealized-gains and wealth taxes). Themes searched in the 2026-11-23 pass: healthcare, taxes, labor, social issues (abortion, same-sex marriage, DEI), climate, foreign policy (Ukraine, NATO, Israel), basic income, patents, education, campaign finance, courts, crypto; no stated position found on most of these beyond the answers recorded.
